title: Global Non-Linearly Stable Large-Data Solutions to the Einstein Scalar Field System
kind: primary research preprint; verbatim TeX-source reading of selected loci (abstract, footnote 1, Definitions 2.4-2.6, Theorems 3.1/3.3, Sections 5-7)
version: arXiv:2108.13377v1, submitted Mon 30 Aug 2021 17:00:03 UTC (only arXiv version; related published DOI 10.1007/s00023-022-01162-4, Ann. Henri Poincaré, not accessed)
locator: TeX nonlin_stab.tex (arXiv e-print 2108.13377v1): abstract lines 106-110; Introduction incl. footnote 1 at line 136 (first of 4 footnotes); Definition 2.4 charinit line ~322; Definition 2.5 asymflat lines 333-343 with weighted displays at TeX lines 336-339; Definition 2.6 localbvscat lines 346-361; constants convention line 356; Theorem 3.1 main1 lines 507-525; Remark 3.2 line 526-528; Theorem 3.3 main2 line 530-533; region definitions Q, O_R, I after line 343; §6 gauge lemmas lines 1359-1431; §7 Regularity Near the Axis lines 1751-1910: Remark 7.1, Proposition 7.2, Lemma 7.3, Corollary 7.4 (XboundCor, hypothesis 'asymptotically flat of order omega'>=2 in C^{2k} towards I^+'), Lemma 7.5 (axisregextra), Corollary 7.6 (Xboundavgcor); Luk-Oh criterion restatement: Definition 'Dispersive Spacetime Solution of Size (C,gamma0,N)' lines 415-450 with items (D1)-(D8), Theorem* 'Large Data Stability, Luk & Oh' lines 456-460
assumptions: Theorem 3.1 hypothesis verbatim: '(phi,r,m) be a locally scattering solution to (SSESF) with initial data asymptotically flat of order omega' >= 2 in C^k (k >= 1) towards I^+ and I^-'. Definition 2.5: sup_{C_1} v^{omega'+l} |partial_v^{l+1}(rphi)| <= A and sup_{underline C_R} (1+|u|)^{omega'+l} |partial^{l+1}(rphi)| <= A' for all l <= k (second display printed with partial_v, prose parenthetical says partial_u). Definition 2.6 local scattering: (3+1) solution future causally geodesically complete plus two BV-type integrals over C_u ∩ {r <= r_0} tending to 0 as u -> infinity.
conclusion: Theorem 3.1: ten families of all-order decay estimates (|alpha| <= k, |beta| <= k+1) on lambda, nu, phi, m, m/r^l, rphi over I = {v >= |u|}, with implicit constants depending on the data constants A, A', |alpha|, |beta|, initial Bondi mass and low-order solution behavior. Theorem 3.3: k >= 11 gives a dispersive spacetime solution of size (C,gamma0,k), hence Luk-Oh future nonlinear stability.
proof_status: Statements and scope read verbatim at full-text depth from the TeX; the §4-§5 induction, its constants and the stability proof were NOT audited. This record verifies hypothesis wording, domain, and constant-dependence only; it is not a proof audit and attributes no correctness claim.
open_questions: Whether the published Ann. Henri Poincaré version changes Definition 2.5's second display (partial_v vs partial_u) or the constants paragraph
Whether the unquantified 'low order behavior' constant dependence could be refined to a quantitative A-dependence
relevance: Primary source for resolving the selected-full-text vs abstract-level Kilgore scope tension: footnote 1 verbatim confirms exclusion of direct control of LOY past-null-infinity scattering spacetimes; Definitions 2.5-2.6 and the constants convention show the hypothesis obstruction for the compact smooth incoming-profile family.
limits: Statement-level verification only; no reproduction of the all-order induction. Published AHP version paywalled, not fetched. Equation-number count in section 2 puts the Definition 2.5 displays at (2.5)-(2.6) (the coordinator register's '(2.4)' appears to count the Remark 2.1 gauge-transform display; harmless locator discrepancy). Definition 2.5's second display uses partial_v where the prose parenthetical introduces partial_u data on underline C_R; recorded as an apparent v1 inconsistency, no correction invented.

title: Solutions to the Einstein-scalar-field system in spherical symmetry with large bounded variation norms
kind: primary research preprint; verbatim TeX-source recheck of finite-cone and scattering statements
version: arXiv:1605.03893v1, submitted Thu 12 May 2016 (only arXiv version); published Ann. PDE 4:3 Art. 3 (2018), DOI 10.1007/s40818-017-0038-4 (not accessible this session)
locator: TeX SSESF-LargeBVScat.160512.tex (arXiv e-print 1605.03893v1): Theorem 1.1 thm:main.finite line 351 with data condition 2 d_v(rphi)(u0,v) = Phi(v) and (IDcond) line ~355, geometric bounds (main:geo) d_v r > 1/3, -2/3 < d_u r < -1/6, 2m/r < 1/2; Definition 2.1 def:C1-sol lines ~504-538 and tangential axis conditions (bc4high-d) line ~545; Theorem 1.7 thm:main lines 452-464 (conclusion line 462 prints 'future and past casually geodesically complete' [sic] and scattering limits lim_{u->-inf} 2 d_v(rphi) = Phi(v), lim d_v r = 1/2); Proposition prop:high-d line 1795 (third pure normalized derivatives, bounds (est4dvdvdvrphi)/(est4dvdvdvr) v-side and (est4dududurphi)/(est4dududur) u-side) with line 1982 'we only sketch the argument' and line 1984 literal '\begin{proof}[Sketch of proof of (est4dududurphi) and (est4dududur)]'; commented-out second-order u-side alternative block lines 1760-1784 (inactive); active second-order u-side proof ends line ~1756; section 4 uniform display lines 2044-2051 (three sums k=0..2 bounding phi, d(rphi), and d^{k+1} r by A+eps and eps(A+eps)); Arzela-Ascoli convergence lines 2052-2060 ((phi, d_v(rphi), d_u(rphi)) -> in C^1, r -> in C^2, m -> in C^1 on compact Omega); Remark line 2081-2090 weak third-derivative bounds; incoming recovery (main:pf:id) line ~2075 with n->infinity first, then u->-infinity
assumptions: Theorem 1.1: data Phi smooth on [u0,infinity) with (IDcond): integral_u^v |Phi| <= eps (v-u)^{1-gamma}, |Phi|+|Phi'| <= eps. Theorem 1.7: Phi smooth on R with (IDcond) for all -infinity < u <= v and sup |Phi''| < infinity; epsilon depends on gamma only (u0-uniform).
conclusion: Theorem 1.1: unique global future-causally-geodesically-complete finite-cone solution with uniform a priori bounds; Theorem 1.7: two-sided complete scattering solution with prescribed profile. Section 4: subsequential limit with the stated finite-order convergence on compact quotient sets.
proof_status: Verbatim statement recheck; the u-side third-derivative halves of prop:high-d are confirmed to be an explicitly labeled proof sketch in v1; the section 4 first-r-derivative display is confirmed to contain a k=0 slot (sup |d_v r| + |d_u r| <= eps(A+eps)) inconsistent with the gauge d_v r|_{C_{u_n}} = 1/2 and with (main:geo), while its k=1,2 slots are consistent with prop:high-d and Remark 4.1. Neither the published-version status of the sketch nor of the typo is verified (paywalled).
dependencies: Persistence of regularity for C^2 solutions
open_questions: Whether the published Ann. PDE §3-§4 expands the u-side sketch or fixes the k=0 display
Rate of decay of d_u(rphi)(u,v) as u -> -infinity at fixed v (needed for the charitable reading of Kilgore's I^- data display)
relevance: Primary anchor for the project's finite-order inputs and for the audit's per-n hypothesis tests: Theorem 1.7's scattering normalization lim_{u->-inf} 2 d_v(rphi) = Phi(v) is what makes Kilgore's literal I^- weighted-data display fail for nonzero profiles.
limits: v1 only; no access to the published version; no independent reproduction of the full §3 estimates or §6 completeness argument (retained as external inputs per prior records).

title: Global nonlinear stability of large dispersive solutions to the Einstein equations (abstract-level record)

locator: arXiv abstract page, abstract block and submission history
assumptions: Abstract verbatim: 'any regular future causally geodesically complete, asymptotically flat solution to the Einstein-scalar field system which approaches the Minkowski spacetime sufficiently fast for large times is future globally nonlinearly stable'.
